subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should OpenClaw keep the dangerous Host-header origin fallback as an operator-selected break-glass policy, or remove/tighten it for exposed gateways?
rationale: Current source already rejects simple mismatched attacker origins and audits exposed fallback as critical, but changing the remaining Host-header fallback behavior would alter a documented security/config tradeoff that automation should not decide.

options.title: Keep and harden
options.body: Preserve the opt-in fallback while adding any missing defense-in-depth and docs/tests that make the DNS-rebinding/operator risk explicit.

options.title: Remove fallback
options.body: Delete the flag and add any needed doctor/docs migration path for deployments that relied on Host-header origin policy.

options.title: Require an extra browser guard
options.body: Allow Host-header fallback only with a CSRF token, `Sec-Fetch-Site` policy, or equivalent same-site browser proof.

recommendation.title: Keep and harden
recommendation.body: Preserve the opt-in fallback while adding any missing defense-in-depth and docs/tests that make the DNS-rebinding/operator risk explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest history on the origin-policy and security-audit files that define this fallback's product boundary.
